rationale: C07 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template. Written shortly before the child letter, it contains the same campaign-oriented inflation argument: inflation particularly harms pensioners, wage earners, and savers; the preceding period produced an approximately 50 percent cost-of-living increase; the Eisenhower Administration held the increase below 3 percent; and continued sound fiscal and monetary policy would protect the dollar. The child compresses and adapts this material into a personal response. C21 and C16 share the inflation theme and some related rhetoric, but neither matches the child's distinctive statistics, contrasts, affected groups, and policy framing as closely as C07.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Since this Administration took office, the rise in the consumer's cost of living has been held down to less than three percent... [in] the preceding Administration... the cost of living rose almost fifty percent.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Between 1945-1952 inflation had pushed up the cost of living by 50 percent... During the last 3 ½ years, the cost of living has fluctuated within a narrow range--the actual increase since 1952 being less than 3 percent.
shared_material.explanation: The same paired statistics and contrast between administrations form the central evidentiary argument in both letters.

shared_material.child_excerpt: It affects all Americans, but particularly people such as yourself and your husband who either are now retired or are about to retire and must plan to live on limited savings or a fixed pension.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: inflation was robbing every market basket, every old person on a pension, every wage earner, every owner of savings bonds or life insurance or money in the bank.
shared_material.explanation: Both identify essentially the same inflation-sensitive constituencies, with the child tailoring the list to its recipient.

shared_material.child_excerpt: For the wage earner... for the retired person whose savings and pensions must be protected and for all Americans, we will continue our battle to secure a stable dollar.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: To maintain that confidence and to sustain our economic progress we must... keep steady the newly-won soundness of the dollar... This Administration will continue to conduct our national affairs so that an owner of a small business can truly say something 'is sound as a dollar.'
shared_material.explanation: Both conclude the inflation discussion with a pledge to continue Administration policy in order to preserve a sound or stable dollar.
